headline: DSA leader calls idea of Ocasio-Cortez presidency ‘exciting,’ says 2028 plans aren’t settled
author: Suryatapa Chakraborty

paragraphs.text: A leader of the Democratic Socialists of America called the possibility of New York Democrat Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s possible run for 2028 White House bid “exciting.”

“People across the country are so excited for the possibility of a president who is going to lead on transformative policies like Medicare for all, expanding worker rights, shifting resources from endless war and militarism to fund our communities right here at home,” said Ashik Siddique, national co-chair of DSA during a Fox News interview.
“It’s really exciting to think about somebody who can really channel the fears that so many people have about the direction of this country,” he added.

The co-chair cautioned that the DSA has not officially made an endorsement yet and that the organization will follow its internal process already in place to get input from members across the country. However, he said that the group is expected to make an official decision by Spring next year.
“When DSA makes an endorsement, it really means something,” Siddique said. “We have a truly democratic process that our members can engage with.”

Earlier this year, the New York City chapter of the DSA formally encouraged Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028, according to a report from the New York Times. The resolution, which was not an official endorsement, passed by a margin of 291 to 123.

The discussion surrounding the 2028 Democratic nominee for White House have begun after the party secured a sweeping victory in the midterm elections, taking control of both chambers of Congress. Democrats flipped GOP-held seats in battleground states like Texas, Mississippi, Alaska, Kansas, Iowa, Maine and more.

Earlier this week, political commentator Scott Jennings encouraged Sens.-elect James Talarico (Texas) and Scott Colom (Miss.) to run for president after their stunning victories in the historically red-leaning states.
“This guy just flipped Texas. If he were smart, he’d be in the presidential campaign right now,” Jennings said, referring to Talarico.

Several names from the Democratic Party — including Ocasio-Cortez, California Gov. Gavin Newsom and Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff — have been floated as potential 2028 candidates. Despite the speculation, none of them have officially announced a bid.
